provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: In the generator the grid has a zero border and zero separator lines at every index that is a multiple of 3. The extent along that axis is 3*pillars+1. These lines split the grid into two-cell-thick strips of colour 8 with random 0 holes. A 2x2 pink (6) block sits in one strip, starting at an index congruent to 1 mod 3. In the generator's frame, the pink box sits at row brow. Its upper and lower loops step away from it two cells at a time. At step j they recolour 8 to 4 in every strip within distance j of the pink strip, except the pink strip itself. So in a strip at distance d>=1, a cell stays 8 only if its coordinate along the strip lies within the pink's span widened by 2*(d-1) on each side. All other 8 cells become 4. This matches the archived solver and all fixtures. The canonical generator randomly transposes its scenes, so orientation cannot come from d4 alone. The emitted program reads it from the visible pixels. It tests which axis has all-palette[0] lines at indices 0,3,6,... with the right length (n%3==1), and checks that the pink starts at an index congruent to 1 mod 3 on that axis. If the evidence is ambiguous or missing, it falls back to counting interior all-zero lines, as the archived solver does. The rule is symmetric under reflection (the cone is two-sided and grows equally), and D4 maps index%3==0 lines to index%3==0 lines because n-1 is a multiple of 3. So a single direct-coordinate program works for every d4. There are explicit row-strip and column-strip branches; nothing is transposed or rotated. Colour roles are fixed constants: palette[0] for separators and holes, palette[8] for the strip body, palette[6] for pink, and palette[4] for the recolour.
draft_notes.limitations: Demonstrations are not consulted, because the rule is fully determined by the generator's structure. Orientation could be ambiguous if both axes show complete periodic zero separators and the pink is aligned on both. That needs random holes to black out entire perpendicular lines, which is astronomically unlikely. In that case the program falls back to interior zero-line counting, and on a tie it picks horizontal strips. If no periodic separator structure is found, strips are found as runs of lines that are not all zero. That fallback would miss a strip that is entirely holes, which is also vanishingly unlikely. The analysis assumes common.get_pixel/draw return a non-8 value for out-of-range coordinates rather than wrapping negative indices. All fixtures are consistent with that, and with the uniform cone rule. No fixture contradictions or constructor tie-break defects were found.
